Brief Hospital Course:
BRIEF HOSPITAL COURSE:
___ yo M with PMH of obesity p/w sub-acute onset of DOE, ___ 
edema, and weight gain over several weeks. He had not received 
any medical care for at least the last ___ years prior to 
admission and was diagnosed with DMII on admission. Pt was 
tachycardic on admission and EKG demonstrated atrial flutter 
with 2:1 conduction, as he perceived no palpitations it was 
unclear how long he had been in this rhythm. Echo showed diffuse 
global hypokinesis with LVEF=30%. Cath done to rule-out ischemic 
source of cardiomyopathy demonstarted no CAD. Further work-up 
for cardiomyopathy was negative; it was ultimately attributed to 
tachy-myopathy in the setting of long-standing undetected atrial 
flutter. Cardioversion failed as pt remained in sinus rhythm for 
only 6 days and then reverted to flutter. Subsequent atrial 
flutter ablation was successful. Over the course of his hospital 
stay pt was diuresed approximately 30 Liters. 
.
HOSPITAL COURSE BY PROBLEM:
# New Diagnosis of Systolic Congestive Heart Failure: Echo of EF 
30% with diffuse global hypokinesis. All studies sent for 
potential causes of cardiomyopathy were negative. Pt did endorse 
a distant hx of alcohol abuse and a current consumption of ___ 
portions of hard-liquour per week which did not seem sufficient 
to account for degree of cardiomyopathy. As he had no perception 
of palpitations and had not received medical care for over one 
decade, the most likely etiology for his cardiomyopathy was felt 
to be tachy-myopathy secondary to longstanding undetected atrial 
flutter. He was massively fluid overloaded on presentation 
demonstrated by pronounced pitting edema and venous stasis of 
the lower extremities, sacrum and abdomen.  PCWP on right heart 
cath was 45.  Initial attempts at diuresis with lasix by bolus 
failed, but lasix drip augmented with intermittent doses of 
metolazone achieved 30L+ of diuresis with corresponding weight 
loss from 400 to 320 pounds. ACEi & Beta-blocker were initiated 
and continued at the time of discharge. Discharge dose of 
lasix=40mg bid. In addition to appts with cardiology and EP, 
arrangements were made for the pt to be followed in heart 
failure clinic.
.  
# CAD: Mildly elevated initial troponin at presentation likely 
due to demand ischemia from CHF exacerbation as above and renal 
insufficiency. Trop=0.03 x 3 with no MB elevation. Cardiac cath 
showed no significant coronary dz. Pt discharged on ASA 81mg for 
primary prevention given his DMII.
.  
# Rhythm: Pt in atrial flutter with 2:1 conduction on admission. 
As above, he may have been in this rhythm for quite some time 
and it was felt to be the source of his tachy-myopathy. 
Cardioversion was initially successful, but pt remained in sinus 
rhythm for only 6 days. Subsequent AF ablation was susccessful. 
Pt was discharged in sinus rhythm. He was started on coumadin 
(to be follwed in ___ clinic) with a lovenox bridge. 
Follow-up was scheduled with EP.
.  
# DM: HbA1C at 11.6 on admission. Initial blood sugars in high 
300s without gap. ___ consult followed pt throughout his 
hospital stay and Insulin regimen was aggressively up-titrated. 
No oral agents were started. Discharge regimen was lantus 55 
units qhs + humalog sliding scale. Follow-up was arranged with 
___.
.  
# ACUTE RENAL FAILURE: Initial Cr suggested normal renal 
function, but diuresis resulted in Cr increase to 1.7 prior to 
d/c. Urinalysis unrevealing. This was attributed to contrast 
received on multiple studies and aggresive diuresis. Pt may have 
some degree of underlying diabetic kidney dz as duration of his 
DMII is unknown. PCP aware of need to repeat renal function at 
two weeks.
.
# SUSPICION FOR OSA: Pt does not carry diagnosis of obstructive 
sleep apnea, but several apneic episodes at night noted by staff 
during this admission. Pt referred for outpt sleep study. As he 
had normal PA pressures on cath, this was not feltr to be a 
likely etiology of his heart failure.

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  ___ male with shortness of breath and lower extremity edema,
to assess for cardiopulmonary process.

TECHNIQUE:  AP and lateral radiographs of the chest were performed.  There is
no relevant prior imaging for comparison.

FINDINGS:

The heart is enlarged.  There is generalized pulmonary venous congestion. 
There is no focal pulmonary consolidation.

CONCLUSION:

The overall findings are consistent with CHF.  Please ensure followup
radiography post-treatment to ensure complete clearance.

INDICATION:  ___ female with obesity, dyspnea on exertion and
tachycardia.  Rule out pulmonary embolism.

COMPARISON:  None.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT-acquired axial images of the chest were obtained without and
with IV contrast per the non-gated chest pain protocol.  Multiplanar
reformations and maximum intensity projection reformations were obtained.

FINDINGS:  There are several prominent mediastinal lymph nodes; however, none
of which meet CT criteria for pathology.  The heart is moderately enlarged.
The aorta is of normal caliber with no evidence of dissection.  The pulmonary
arteries are normal with no evidence of pulmonary embolism.  Apart from linear
atelectasis within the left lingula and upper lobe, the lungs are clear. There
are tiny bilateral pleural effusions. Ther is no pericardial effusion.

Limited views of the upper abdomen are unremarkable.

There are no osseous lesions worrisome for malignancy.  There are moderate
degenerative changes of the thoracic spine.

IMPRESSION:

1.  No evidence of pulmonary embolism.  No evidence of pneumonia.
2.  Small bilateral pleural effusions.
